newsitem.title: TURKEY: Kurd party gives murder files to Turkish probe.
newsitem.headline: Kurd party gives murder files to Turkish probe.

text.p: A Kurdish political party on Monday gave information on more than a 140 mystery killings to a Turkish parliamentary inquiry probing alleged links between security officials and far-right hitmen, party officials said.

"We asked our supporters to give us any information they could on the mystery killings and today we passed the files on to the commission," People's Democracy Party (HADEP) deputy chairman Sedat Yurtdas told Reuters.
The issue of unsolved political killings has come into the limelight since a security scandal broke last November.
An intelligence service official and a former rightist convict have told the inquiry set up to probe the scandal that the state used far-right gangsters for political dirty work.
Human rights activists say around 3,500 civilians, mostly Kurds, have been killed mysteriously in 12 years of conflict between troops and Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels in southeast Turkey.
Yurtdas said his party had passed on information on 148 of the most detailed cases to the inquiry and told MPs that HADEP held the security forces responsible for many of the killings.

"(The killers) can take the form of officals, civilians, Hizbullah or repentant PKK members but it all comes down to the fact that there are gangs who have set up their stall inside the state," he said.
The armed Islamist group Hizbullah has killed dozens of Kurdish rebel sympathisers in the southeast in the 1990s. Many Kurds suspect the group of having official links.
More than 21,000 people have died in the fighting in the mainly Kurdish southeast.
